scope: Round 2: the six keys changed by the D2/D3 copy round. The rest of the namespace was audited in an earlier round and is out of scope here.

findings.detail: «ایجنٹ کے مالکان» renders the English class term 'agent owners' as the owners of this one agent; «ایجنٹس کے مالکان» (the app already uses «ایجنٹس» for agents, e.g. ui.agents.publication.team_plan_required.body) would state the class. Left open deliberately: the singular reading is a defensible statement of the rule for the chief of staff this audit covers, and widening what a disclosure says other people may read is the manager's call, not a unilateral auditor edit.

resolved_findings.detail: Bare verb clause with an ambiguous «یہ»: it can parse as subject (the names below → 'these can also read') or as object («can also read this», addressed to the reader), so in a header it can read back as an echo of the disclosure's «آپ یہ آڈٹ پڑھ سکتے ہیں» instead of a label naming the other readers — the exact D2 regression this key exists to avoid. Fixed: «یہ بھی پڑھ سکتے ہیں» → «یہ افراد بھی پڑھ سکتے ہیں» (explicit subject, still a short metadata label with «بھی» = also, no colon, no placeholder, no sentence-final stop).

The ownership basis put its relative clause after the copula («…اس چیف آف اسٹاف کے مالک آپ ہیں جس کا یہ آڈٹ ہے»), a colloquial afterthought order that reads as clumsy in a written disclosure. Reordered to the standard relative-first Urdu form; both required facts kept (own-basis, and that other members are told agent owners can audit) and no exclusivity claim added. Fixed: «آپ یہ آڈٹ پڑھ سکتے ہیں کیونکہ اس چیف آف اسٹاف کے مالک آپ ہیں جس کا یہ آڈٹ ہے۔» → «آپ یہ آڈٹ پڑھ سکتے ہیں کیونکہ جس چیف آف اسٹاف کا یہ آڈٹ ہے، اس کے مالک آپ ہیں۔»
